links.outcome: Readability of chatbot dyspepsia responses versus sixth-grade patient education standard
links.effect: None of the four chatbots met the sixth-grade standard; ARI, GFI, FKGL, CLI and SMOG exceeded thresholds and FRES fell below threshold for all models.
links.quote: None of the models met the prespecified sixth-grade reading standard for patient education materials.

links.outcome: Plain-language comprehensibility of AI-generated patient health information
links.effect: All four chatbots produced text with high reading difficulty; readability indices exceeded recommended thresholds across models.
links.quote: ARI, GFI, FKGL, CLI, and SMOG values exceeded the recommended thresholds for all models, whereas FRES values were below the recommended threshold, indicating high reading difficulty overall.

screen.reason: Empirical cross-sectional benchmark comparing four mainstream LLM chatbots on quality and readability metrics for dyspepsia patient questions, but does not test an organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
